measurements.note: n=200, d=3, |E|=300. Hakimi realisation + 5·2·|E|=3_000 MCMC proposals + windowed connectivity checks every max(16, 2|E|=600) proposals.
n=600, d=3, |E|=900. 9_000 MCMC proposals. ~5.4x time for 3x n — MCMC chain length scales linearly in |E|, connectivity-guard cost adds super-linear factor due to BFS over growing graph.
n=1200, d=3, |E|=1_800. 18_000 MCMC proposals. ~3.4x time for 2x n. Confirms quasi-linear scaling in |E| for the MCMC body, dominated by per-window BFS connectivity rechecks.

n=200, skewed sequence (4 vertices of degree 10, 168 of degree 3, 28 of degree 2; Σd=600, |E|=300). MCMC rejection rate is higher because the 4 high-degree stubs collide often, but per-rejection cost is cheap (no rollback). Net wall-clock is below the regular n=200 case because realisation finds many connectable edges quickly.

cross_reference.note: C upstream wraps the same routine in igraph_degree_sequence_game(IGRAPH_DEGSEQ_VL). Single-threaded by design; no parallelism. Our impl uses SplitMix64 (non-portable), so absolute medians here are not comparable to igraph C's libc rand()-based path — they characterize the Rust implementation only.

interpretation.primary_cost: MCMC edge-swap chain (5·2·|E| proposals) + periodic O(|V|+|E|) BFS connectivity checks every max(16, 2|E|) proposals.
interpretation.rust_advantages: Hakimi-based connected realisation prior is O(Σd log Σd) and runs once. No allocation inside the inner swap loop: snapshot vectors are reused.
interpretation.future_optimisations: 1) Track connectivity incrementally via link-cut trees instead of full-BFS rollback windows (cuts the dominant cost for large |E|). 2) Bias proposal distribution toward stubs not recently touched to lower rejection rate on power-law-tailed inputs.
